searchText: Is t8ntool in the Docker image? I can't find it there, only the config/t8ntool dir But why run both? Isn't this running the same tests in 2 (slightly different?) ways? By the way, FYI, for our EVM project we are finding more useful the BlockchainTests files because they contain details like storage and are easier to understand. The GeneralStateTests require state hashes which we don't implement. What is the recommended configuration for running the tests with the Docker image? My Podman installation (alternative to Docker) creates by default a 1 CPU, 2 GB RAM machine 2 gb ram is not enough T8ntool is geth interface. It runs with `evm t8n ` Yes it is in docker. You can make your evm to support the same interface and I make a config to run with retesteth Devs insisted on keeping the state test format, as its convenient for them So how do I run `t8ntool -t BlockchainTests -- --all -j2 --filltests` with the Docker image? OK, but if I run the BCGeneralStateTests, there is no advantage in running the GeneralStateTests, right? (nor viceversa) No, it must be exactly the same. I verify the hashes when filling Here are the manuals https://ethereum-tests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/retesteth-ref.html Or you want to run geth evm t8n directly? Then you need to manually prepare input text files with env, transactions, state and run it with geth yes, I read that, but there are no examples to run `t8ntool`. Only retesteth. Sorry for all the questions, I'm just trying to understand everything. Retesteth by default execute tests using geth t8ntool http://tinyurl.com/2ctak8yn Here is the test diagram I mean... I know how to run `evm t8n` and `retesteth`. But there is no executable for `t8ntool`, right? evm t8n is t8ntool What is it you're trying to do? ok, so t8ntool is whatever you call from config/t8ntool/start.sh Yes. By default the config is t8ntool. But in folder config/default If you just investigate how it all function we can have a call I was trying to replicate the same results that are shown in http://retesteth.ethdevops.io/ . For geth-t8ntool it shows a command line like `t8ntool -t BlockchainTests -- ...`, so that's what I was trying to do --config t8ntool After -- But it is already the results for geth The info on page is shrinked to fit, it is not the actual command aha, that's what explains everything 🙂 Another thing: the tests in BlockchainTestFiller/ValidBlocks/ are generated by scripts in src/Templates/BadOpcode. That is confusing, because there is an existing but unrelated set of tests also named BadOpcode. Probably the scripts folder should be renamed to src/Templates/ValidBlocks? Thats Oris thing. The template scripts generate fillers in src/BlockchainTests/ValidBlocks/bcBadOpcode (or similar path) Yes its weird, we now have fillers for the fillers <@439556036647714817> I see GeneralStateTests/stBadOpcode, but those seem to be unrelated to the scripts and ValidBlocks Which test in blockchain is generated by trmplate script you say? src/Templates/BadOpcode/createOpcodeTest.sh creates fillers in BlockchainTestsFiller/ValidBlocks/bcStateTests/ (if you want I can make a GitHub issue with this) Ah, here this ones https://github.com/ethereum/tests/blob/develop/src/Templates/BadOpcode/createOpcodeTest.sh yes What's the issue? it's confusing that the BadOpcode templates do not create BadOpcode tests 🙂 they create something else Yes, we took a moment to find it (I don't really mind, I just thought it might help if I report it) Do you have more questions? not for now... I am now increasing the shm to try to get the vmtraces
